rule: Beekeeper is a work identity; it does not directly grant every feature.
Effective permissions are derived from confirmed capabilities + policy + workspace/resource scope.
Hive-centric: manage, inspect, observe, capture evidence and review hive history.
Bee Health Scan is enabled only when the user confirms frame/colony screening work.
Connected Hive Monitoring is enabled only when the user confirms use of connected sensors.
Honey Collection is enabled only when the user confirms harvesting/collection work.
Device Management is a technical extension; not shown by default.
Navigation changes compositionally with capabilities; do not show empty role modules.
Dashboard modules are permission/data driven, not a single hardcoded Beekeeper dashboard.
Quality, Processing, Packaging, Verification, Distribution, QR management and technical proof are not Beekeeper defaults.
Backend authorization is authoritative; frontend visibility is not an authorization boundary.
Processor is a facility production identity; it does not directly grant Hive management or Quality decisions.
Permissions are derived from confirmed processing capabilities + policy + workspace scope.
Batch intake, centrifugal extraction, settling tank logs, evidence capture and batch advancement.
Batch Split / Merge is enabled only when multi-lot combining is confirmed.
Processor prepares Quality Handoffs but cannot certify or make quality pass/fail decisions.
Processor prepares Packaging Handoffs but does not generate consumer QR identities without packaging authority.
Lab is a laboratory work identity; it does not automatically grant every Quality, Verification or Packaging action.
Receive/identify samples, perform configured tests, record results and preserve laboratory evidence.
Entering or reviewing a laboratory result is distinct from a final business quality decision.
Lab capabilities do not automatically grant QUALITY_DECISION, BATCH_VERIFY or release authority.
Lab users see only the batch/source context necessary for authorized testing.
Original test evidence and result history should be preserved; edits require audit history.
The system must not invent laboratory readings, limits, certifications or pass/fail outcomes.
Instrument/equipment controls are optional extensions and should not appear for every Lab user.
Dashboard modules are composed from capabilities, permissions, pending samples and actual lab data.
Backend authorization is authoritative; frontend hiding is not a security control.
Dispatch/Distributor describes distribution work; it does not automatically grant Packaging, Quality, Verification or financial authority.
Move eligible packaged products from dispatch planning through delivery confirmation while preserving traceability.
Inventory visibility does not grant permission to edit package production or packaging records.
Distributor can view permitted batch/product lineage but cannot alter upstream hive, collection, processing or quality records.
Viewing public verification is different from creating/revoking QR records or performing batch verification.
Recipient/customer data must be scoped to the user's workspace and operational need.
Proof of delivery must represent actual evidence; the system must not fabricate signatures, locations or timestamps.
Returns do not automatically modify batch verification or quality status; downstream workflows must determine the effect.
Compose the dashboard from actual distribution capabilities, pending work and shipment state.
Backend authorization is authoritative; frontend visibility is not the security boundary.
